newsitem.title: CANADA: Domco shares jump on Armstrong bid.
newsitem.headline: Domco shares jump on Armstrong bid.

text.p: Shares of Domco Inc jumped 7.65 to 22.40 on Monday after Armstrong World Industries Inc said it was planning to offer C$488 million cash or C$23 a share for the Canadian floor-covering manufacturer.
Domco, based in Farnham, Quebec, about 80 miles (130 km) east of Montreal, is 57 percent-controlled on a fully diluted basis by Sommer Allibert S.A. of France.
"Our offer is a terrific offer for Domco shareholders," Armstrong Chief Executive George Lorch said in a telephone conference call with reporters on Monday.
"We are seriously interested in acquiring Domco," he said.

Armstrong said its bid would include an offer for Domco's convertible debentures, warrants and other convertible securities on an equivalent basis. The bid is conditional on receiving two-thirds of the outstanding shares on a fully-diluted basis.
"This offer is not conditional on financing. That is already in place," Lorch said.
Armstrong was prepared to meet with Sommer officials and preferred to make a negotiated transaction for Domco, he said.

Armstrong's offer came after Sommer announced on May 28 that it would enter into a leveraged business combination with Tarkett A.G., a German floor manufacturer. Tarkett offered US$562 million for all of Sommer's flooring assets, which include Domco, Armstrong said.
Armstrong said Tarkett's offer was "substantially less than the amount proposed by Armstrong on a comparable basis."
"Under the Sommer/Tarkett transaction, there is absolutely no value being provided for Domco shareholders," Lorch said in the conference call.
Sommer had rejected an earlier offer from Armstrong to purchase all of its flooring and wall covering business, including Domco, Armstrong said.
Domco trades on the Toronto and Montreal stock exchanges.

Domco is the leading Canadian manufacturer and distributor of sheet vinyl and vinyl composition floorcoverings, and also distributes carpets and floorcovering accessories made by other companies. Domco's U.S. subsidiary is incorporated in Wilmington, Delaware.
